notes: Corrected: both ... and is now one discontinuous unit on the waw, headed on and, and the first min keeps only its own of. Rule 14's default gives a correlative pair written for one connective morpheme to that morpheme; its exception hands the opening word to another morpheme only where that morpheme is itself what the correlative says, as the min of a min ... 'ad range is. Here the phrase is two parallel partitives, the ASV writes an of for each, and rule 14 states in terms that a morpheme merely standing where the opening correlative stands has no claim on it — the reasoning that leaves the two lamedhs of la-zakhar 'o la-neqevah without the whether.
The superlative qodshey ha-qodashim is divided most / holy between rectum and construct; the reverse division remains defensible and is named in the unit's note.
The article on ha-qodashim takes the the standing before its own word under rule 29, and the second min keeps its own of.
